newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens further on dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens further on dollar demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling eased further on Thursday as the market experienced a surge in dollar demand from local investors, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.74 against the dollar from 54.71, while against the pound it was posted at 88.80 from 90.99.
Dealers said this demand was not from the traditional importers -- normally oil, motor and manufacturing industries but was seen to come from local individual investors.
"There is some speculation in the market that the government's recent announcement to lift the maize import ban on Tuesday has sparked off some dollar-buying interest," one dealer said.

The lifting of the maize ban means that anyone with a trading licence can now import maize into the country: "And since it is an immediate need, most traders are opting out of the normal import financing channels because they take longer to process," he added.
Another dealer said that what the market was seeing was a slight correct of the shilling dollar inflows were still coming in from the oil sector & foreign investors looking to buy treasury bills.
"The central bank is buying all the excess dollars, most probably to keep the shilling at a stable rate," he said.
"The next test for the shilling should be the 54.90 level, which market sentiment across the board appears to favor," dealers said.
The money market was tight with most banks holding onto their funds to lend only at high rates. Overnight rates were quoted at above 25 percent levels unchanged from Wednesday.
